provenance.note: `Schemas` takes a whole `SignifyClient`, so the real client is driven with `globalThis.fetch` replaced by a recorder that signs its answers as a KERIA agent would. The clock and the agent's key are pinned. The two schema SAIDs are the vLEI ones the integration tests use, so the recorded paths are the ones a real deployment sees. `PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL`: the passcode is the pinned tests' own and has never protected anything.

declarations.schema_type: Schema: { $id: string; $schema: string; title: string; description: string; type: string; credentialType: string; version: string; properties: { [key: string]: unknown; }; additionalProperties: boolean; required: string[]; };

notes.segment: both paths use the **singular** `/schema`, not `/schemas`, while the accessor and the class are plural — an easy thing to get wrong and the reason this port pins the segment as a constant
notes.encoding: `get` interpolates the SAID straight into the path with no encoding, as every other family in this file does
notes.list: `list` addresses a constant path, so it is the second endpoint in the port whose address carries no caller input
notes.response: both return `res.json()` with no validation, typed as `Schema` at compile time only

pinned_confirmations.note: no pinned unit test exercises either call: `clienting.test.ts` asserts the accessor's type and nothing else. The only real usage is `test-integration/credentials.test.ts`, which reads both vLEI schemas by SAID and asserts each answer's `$id`, then lists and asserts a count — so what upstream actually checks is that a schema comes back under the SAID it was asked for. Both SAIDs are recorded here and both are valid qualified digests, which is what lets this port take a `Said` rather than a string.

the_said_is_not_encoded.note: `get` interpolates its SAID straight into the path, so a value carrying `/`, `?`, or `#` addresses a different resource — and Roadmap 3.10 signs `@path`, so it changes what a signature commits to
the_said_is_not_encoded.rust_decision: refused twice over: the argument is Roadmap 3.3's validated `Said` rather than a string, and Roadmap 5.3's builder would encode it exactly once even if it were not. A qualified digest's alphabet is URL-safe Base64, so every real SAID reaches the path byte-identical.

the_segment_is_singular.note: both paths address `/schema`, singular, while the class, the accessor, and the roadmap item are all plural — the one place in this file where the resource name and its accessor disagree
the_segment_is_singular.rust_decision: reproduced exactly, and pinned as a named constant so the plural module name cannot drift into the path

the_answer_is_never_validated.note: `get` returns `res.json()` cast to `Schema`, so an answer carrying only `$id` — missing all nine other required fields — is handed to the caller as a schema. The type exists at compile time only.
the_answer_is_never_validated.rust_decision: decoded: an answer that is not a `Schema` is `ClientError::Api`. The wrong-shaped answer recorded here is proven refused.

a_listing_carries_no_input.note: `list` addresses a constant path with no filter, range, or paging of any kind, so an agent holding many schemas returns all of them in one body
a_listing_carries_no_input.rust_decision: reproduced; the response is bounded only by Roadmap 5.1's transport limit, which is recorded as a limitation rather than a filter this port invents

nothing_checks_the_said_came_back.note: the reference's own integration test asserts `schema.$id` equals the SAID it asked for, which is the check that matters — but `Schemas.get` itself does not make it, so a misrouted or substituted answer is returned unchallenged
nothing_checks_the_said_came_back.rust_decision: reproduced rather than fixed: `get` returns what the agent sent and a caller compares. Inventing the check would diverge from the reference for a guarantee only a digest verification can actually give, which is Roadmap 3.3's job and not an endpoint's.
